capacity.baseline_source: 270687657 (capacity API and cache guards, before reservation use)
capacity.protocol: Three alternating AB/BA pairs per compiler runtime and corpus. Equal-length paths; fresh cache per pair/variant, cold then warm; same current input sources and RC output; checker/AST/body caches disabled, production module caches enabled; Node wrapper with inlining. No concurrent local build/test/measurement.

notes: The cache comparison includes the new builtin API as well as the cache guards. Cold allocation rises by 243728 bytes; warm allocation falls by 798376 bytes. It is not a claim that every warm compiler build reuses bodies.

The capacity comparison starts after the API/guard changes; the only compiler algorithm change is pruner output reservation. Both compiler runtimes and every temperature/pair emit byte-identical targets.

After three pairs, all bump CLI warm pairs were slower. Three further alternating pairs were collected for that condition, not substituted for the first batch. Their cold ratios are +1.7%, +0.5%, -0.6% and warm ratios +2.9%, +1.9%, -1.2%. All samples are retained.

The same-artifact A/A control has equal heap, capacity and output within every pair, but wall deltas range from -48.5% to +1.7%. No reliable wall-time speedup is established; the initial bump CLI warm regression must not be hidden by pooling.

The initial CLI attempt stopped at contract validation because generated source bundles were missing. Full bundle generation was completed before any valid CLI sample; the closure dependency list contains none of those generated bundles, so its existing samples remain valid.
RSS is the runner end-of-run RSS, not a measured peak. Heap pointer is allocation high water for bump and a main-heap measure for RC; neither is live bytes.
